title: Anime/manga platform: art-led bento panels with inverse corners
contains_third_party_content: Anime artwork (a red-haired character close-up), a thumbnail with anime characters, Instagram and YouTube logos, a dog photo.

observed.layout: A taupe frame over a blurred ground. A large central rounded panel holds a close-up of a red-haired anime face. A notched tab at the top center carries ANIME / MANGA / CHAT. A frosted top-right tile 'NEW EPISODE 8 MAR'. Left column of separate rounded containers: icon rail (logo, home, star, award), avatar 'PROFILE', chat tile (dog avatar with a mic badge, 'CHAT', red circle with a down arrow), socials (Instagram, YouTube) with EN / RU toggles. Bottom right: a 'CONTINUE' button and a video thumbnail with a play button. Two red circular down-arrow buttons.
observed.hierarchy: The hero image first; tile sizes reflect importance.
observed.typography: Small sans labels in light grey. Typeface unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Concave-corner panels, frosted overlays, blur over art.

implementation_notes: Concave corners via masks or pseudo-elements.
Frosted tiles via backdrop-filter over the art.

concept_work.essence: Everything else is a dark frame around one image, and the accent comes from that image.
what_makes_it_work: Notched corners make panels look carved from one slab.
Crimson appears only on actions, tying controls to the art.
gaps_to_make_it_work: 'CHAT' appears both as a top tab and as a tile.
Two identical red arrows have unclear targets; 'NEW EPISODE 8 MAR' has no title or action.

links: The red accent marks scroll and continue actions.
Frosted tiles sit over the art as overlays.

pattern.name: Art-led bento shell with a notched tab
use_when: Media or entertainment where one image sells the page
adaptation_examples: Game launcher: hero is the featured game, accent from its key art.
Music app: hero is the current album, accent from the cover.

lessons: Derive the accent color from the hero image.
Avoid duplicating an entry as both a tab and a tile.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Warm dark taupe panels around one hero image; the crimson accent is taken from the hair in the art and appears only on actions.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: A media platform home, but the main action is unclear beyond the arrows.
Strong hero, cohesive frame and an accent drawn from the art.
Bento and notch conventions are met; duplicate 'CHAT' and ambiguous arrows weaken correctness.
No tab states or arrow targets are shown.
Panels, corner radius and accent are consistent.
The notched bento with art-derived accent is distinctive.

Scored on conservative values: primary text min 4.07:1; secondary text min 3.44:1; icon min 10.19:1; non-color state cue: True. Using best-estimate values the score would be 3; the measurement is within error of a threshold.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
